learnings.question: Who is credited with the influential 1971 observation that in an information-rich world, the growing wealth of information inevitably creates a scarcity of attention?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon, in 1971, argued that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which of these is described, in a hadith found in the 40 Hadith an-Nawawi collection, as part of the perfection of a Muslim's faith?
options: Leaving that which does not concern him
Praying five times a day without delay
learnings.learning: A hadith from the 40 Hadith an-Nawawi collection (narrated by Abu Hurayrah) states that part of the perfection of one's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What is the term for the phenomenon where simply writing information down, or saving it digitally, signals to the brain that it no longer needs to remember it?
options: The Performance Paradox of Cognitive Offloading
learnings.learning: Psychologists call the habit of outsourcing memory to notes or phones the "Performance Paradox" of Cognitive Offloading: the brain treats writing something down as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: Research tracing back to psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus in the 1880s found that, without actively forcing recall, people forget roughly what percentage of newly learned information within just 24 hours?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is why passive re-reading doesn't work as well as being quizzed.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact exists specifically to visualize a Sprint's progress and show how much work remains?
learnings.learning: In Scrum, the Burndown Chart is the artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress, showing remaining work and whether the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three official roles defined in the Scrum framework?
learnings.learning: Scrum defines exactly three roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers. "Project Manager" is not one of Scrum's defined roles.

learnings.question: In this framework for understanding human purpose in Islam, what are identified as the three primary roles that give life meaning?
options: Gaining knowledge, achieving success, and finding happiness
Worshiping Allah, serving as steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter
Seeking wealth, raising a family, and building community
learnings.learning: Life's purpose is framed around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as a steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the eternal Hereafter through accountable choices.

learnings.question: What does the Arabic term "khalifah," used to describe humanity's role on Earth, actually mean?
options: A steward or caretaker (a successive authority)
A judge or ruler over other nations
learnings.learning: "Khalifah" refers to humanity's role as a steward or caretaker (a successive authority) of the Earth, a responsibility that includes preserving faith and unity within the community.

learnings.question: Which principle holds that even a deed as small as "an atom's weight," whether good or evil, will ultimately be seen and accounted for?
options: Divine reward and consequence for every deed, however small
learnings.learning: The principle that "whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it" teaches that no deed, however small, goes unaccounted for.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state is described as a very light sleep, comparable to a computer screen turning off, that can quickly wake up to resume activity?
learnings.learning: The PCIe power state L0s is a very light sleep state, comparable to a computer screen turning off, designed for very short durations of idleness with a quick wake-up.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down, offering the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: The L2 PCIe power state is almost completely powered down, comparable to a computer being fully shut down, giving the highest power savings and the longest wake-up delay of all the states.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life, as opposed to Allah's complete eternal plan?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in a person's life, shaped by their actions and decisions, while Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal knowledge of everything that will happen.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In the Islamic concept of divine decree, what is the relationship between a person's sincere supplication (dua) and the events of their life?
options: Dua can change a person's circumstances (Qada'), but that very change was already known within Allah's eternal plan (Qadr)
Dua has no real effect on what happens in a person's life
Only the supplications of prophets can alter a person's fate
Qadr can be changed by dua, while Qada' is permanently fixed
learnings.learning: Sincere dua can change a person's Qada' (life circumstances), but that change was always already known to Allah and encompassed within His eternal Qadr, since He is All-Knowing.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Contrary to what the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) might suggest, what percentage of the Quran's total text is actually made up of its top 20 most frequently used words?
learnings.learning: A word-frequency analysis of the Quran found that the top 20 most frequent words accumulate to only about 20.83% of the text, so the Pareto Principle's 80/20 pattern does not hold here.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: Roughly what is the ratio of distinct Arabic words to the roughly 170,000 words in the Oxford English Dictionary?
learnings.learning: There are roughly 12 million distinct Arabic words compared to about 170,000 English words in the Oxford English Dictionary, an approximate ratio of 71 Arabic words for every 1 English word.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
